subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Park Deserts: Who Lacks Green Space?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Park Deserts: Who Lacks Green Space?.

hook.text: 100 million Americans — one in three — don't live within a ten-minute walk of a park.

buildup.text: Park access maps reveal a clear pattern: wealthy neighborhoods have parks. Poor ones have parking lots.

discovery.text: The Trust for Public Land's 10-Minute Walk campaign aims to put a park within reach of every American.

twist.text: When parks are built in underserved areas, property values rise and displacement follows. Green gentrification.

climax.text: Cities now pair park construction with anti-displacement policies to keep existing residents in place.

punchline.text: Build a park. Protect the neighbors. The order matters.

quiz.question: What is 'green gentrification'?
options: Planting trees that are invasive species in city parks
New parks raising property values and displacing existing residents
Converting green spaces into commercial developments
